decision_reason: A1 already provides multiple distinctions for jogging and stairs, despite their relatively weak seen coverage. Its closest unseen pairs are eating soup versus eating sandwich and eating soup versus writing. Preserve the existing concepts and add wrist_orientation_variability to distinguish local manipulation from global posture changes. This offers a plausible additional contrast between constrained writing and larger reorienting actions, and between level-preserving food transport and cup tilting. Soup versus sandwich remains potentially ambiguous; food identity and utensil use alone do not justify reliable IMU attributes. The supplied distances guide this refinement but do not establish predictability or recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: wrist_orientation_variability
attributes.definition: Extent of change in the wrist-worn watch's gravity-relative inclination within a window, excluding rotation that leaves inclination unchanged and without interpreting wrist motion as global posture change.

levels.Medium: Wrist inclination changes through a moderate range.
levels.High: Wrist inclination changes through a large range.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports overall acceleration and rotation magnitude. Retains the vigorous-locomotion contrast for jogging and stairs and the low-energy writing anchor. Phone and watch motion provide expected evidence, but limb-dominated motion and carrying style can obscure whole-activity intensity.

cadence: G6 supports repetition rate, preserving transfer from walking to jogging and stairs and from rapid manipulation to slower actions. Repeated phone or watch motion is expected evidence. Pauses, mixed movement cycles and weak periodicity make cadence ambiguous; repetition strength is not repetition rate.

smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid changes rather than isolated impacts. Preserves A1's soup-versus-sandwich distinction and separates controlled manipulation from fluctuating locomotion. Expected evidence is continuity of phone or watch motion; speed, pauses and individual technique can blur this distinction, so it is not treated as a guaranteed separator.

impulsiveness: G10 supports brief abrupt changes associated with foot contacts or ball interactions. Provides transferable impact semantics for jogging and playing catch w/tennis ball. Expected evidence is isolated sharp phone or watch motion; impact transmission, hand cushioning and incidental knocks introduce ambiguity.

posture_inclination: G1 supports static gravity-relative orientation and mean posture. Preserves the sitting-versus-standing distinction and the existing postural context for stairs. The phone may provide indirect body-orientation evidence, but unspecified carrying position and wrist independence limit inference of global load-bearing configuration; no new posture distinctions are asserted.

posture_variability: G12 supports changing gravity-relative posture. Retains global postural adjustment as a distinction between locomotion, ball actions and stationary manipulation. Expected evidence is changing body-coupled phone inclination; phone placement and local limb motion can confound it, and wrist reorientation must not be substituted for global posture change.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular-motion prominence. Retains transferable distinctions among writing, food handling, cup use and throwing actions through expected phone or watch rotation. Rotation magnitude depends on technique and sensor placement; it does not uniquely determine the range of gravity-relative wrist inclination.

translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translational-motion proxies. Preserves walking as the locomotor anchor for jogging and stairs, rather than relying on the superficially nearby eating pasta prototype for stairs. Expected phone motion can support progression, but short windows, drift and stationary limb translation prevent reliable absolute travel or elevation inference.

motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and temporal predictability independently of repetition rate. Preserves transfer from walking to jogging and from structured manipulation to less predictable food or ball actions. Expected evidence is consistency across successive movements; pauses, short windows and individual pacing can obscure class-level regularity.

wrist_orientation_variability: G12, with G1 and G2, supports the range of watch inclination changes, not merely angular speed. Expected evidence is relatively constrained inclination during writing or level-preserving transport versus larger reorientation during cup tilting and object manipulation. This adds a local degree of freedom absent from global posture_variability and can distinguish writing from eating soup beyond intensity, and eating soup from drinking from cup beyond overall rotation and regularity. Seen anchors span constrained desk activity and reorienting manipulation. Grip, writing technique, active versus watch-wearing hand, dynamic acceleration and windows containing only a hold can obscure the distinction. Soup and sandwich may overlap, so no forced separation is claimed.

semantic_redundancy_review: All nine A1 concepts are retained unchanged and accounted for once; the single addition is accounted for once. Intensity measures magnitude, cadence repetition rate, regularity temporal consistency, smoothness sustained fluctuations and impulsiveness isolated abrupt peaks. Mean global inclination differs from global inclination variability. Wrist_orientation_variability is explicitly local and measures inclination range, whereas rotational_motion measures angular-motion prominence and can be high with little inclination change. Translational_motion remains locomotor progression, not local hand displacement. No food identity, utensil identity, stair elevation or fine finger-motion attribute is introduced. Close pairs without a sufficiently reliable additional physical distinction are allowed to remain close.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
